question: Can a library entry discovered in separately synthesized primitive programs lower the total remaining cost on unseen repeated and broken rule structures at three composition depths?
inputs: 24 separately preselected trained rules on four, six and eight essential inputs. Only their exact synthesized primitive program trees and anonymous task identifiers enter fragment mining. Evaluation uses the previous reserved 24 rules on five, seven and nine essential inputs.
forbidden_inputs: Training source formulas, group labels, planted locations, original fold or its truth signature in the learner. No held outcomes before checkpoint freeze. With a frozen library, deployment receives complete target truth and n only.
outputs: A frozen library with zero or one anonymous three-input function, a primitive representative and executable NAND block, every candidate class and support, all training and held searches, exact verification and per-prefix total work.
mapping: Solve every training rule with the cached primitive solver. Across all returned trees, rank adjacent pairs of primitive operations by distinct training-task support under operand permutation, then occurrence count, then truth-byte tie order. Freeze the most recurrent nontrivial candidate seen in two or more different rules. Automatically compile the chosen table to cofactor tests for recursive synthesis on unknown raw operand pairs.
primary_observable: Equal exhaustive correctness. Compare the full cost on the 24 reserved rules, including all discovery, against cached primitive search. Report deterministic search trials and elapsed costs with and without acquisition, and first all-in break-even or end gap. Report depth and matched changes separately.
comparators_or_controls: Direct primitive solver; learned entry callable or fully inlined under identical matching; original fold granted free under the same generic matching procedure. Both cold-per-task and retained within-arity caches.
resource_budget: 24 training tasks and 24 held tasks, each up to 512 held assignments. One fully paid discovery run. Five sequential held timing repeats per each of four methods in each cache mode.
first_executable_signal: Find recurring unnamed fragment(s) in independently solved and verified training programs; record every candidate and whether a reusable entry was selected before opening the test set.
stop_rule: Freeze the actual result of the one prespecified training run. Incur every rejected candidate and failed rule, score all reserved tasks as ordered, and stop. No adaptation to held rules or additional follow-on study.
nonclaims: This is an exploratory, finite test of transfer from a benchmark that contains repeated two-operation motifs. It is not unrestricted abstraction discovery or a theorem about scaling.
